Bloomberg Odd Lots Host Says This May Be the "Coldest Crypto Winter Ever"

Bloomberg Odd Lots host Joe Weisenthal said in his newsletter that this may be the "coldest crypto winter ever." He argued that crypto faces multiple narrative pressures, including fading "we're still early" claims, already-realized institutional adoption and regulatory tailwinds, AI taking market attention and electricity resources, quantum-security concerns around Bitcoin, and DAT firms such as Strategy shifting from buyers to sellers.

Weisenthal also said strong AI and tech-stock rallies are drawing capital and attention away from crypto, while the few crypto winners may have already completed their major moves. The comments represent his personal view. — link

According to SoSoValue data, on June 2 (ET), U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a total net outflow of $519 million, marking 12 consecutive days of outflows. U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs saw a total net outflow of $90.15 million, extending their outflow streak to 16 days. — link

Zcash Foundation released Zebra 4.5.3 and 5.0.0 to fix a critical soundness bug in the Orchard Action circuit. Zebra 4.5.3 temporarily disabled Orchard actions via an emergency soft fork at mainnet block height 3,363,426, while Zebra 5.0.0 activated the NU6.2 hard fork at block height 3,364,600 and re-enabled Orchard with the corrected circuit.

Zcash Foundation said the vulnerability was caught before any known exploitation, with no evidence of unauthorized value creation. User privacy was not affected, and Sapling and transparent transactions continued to operate normally. Zebra node operators are strongly urged to upgrade to 5.0.0. — link

Binance disclosed that it holds a minority stake in Alpaca, which holds approximately 94% market share in the custody of tokenized US stocks and ETFs.

Binance just partners with Alpaca for US stock and ETF trading. Per their agreement, Binance receives 50% of Alpaca’s Payment for Order Flow (PFOF) fees and 65% of the remaining profit from user stock lending after paying interest to users. — link
U.S. ADP employment increased by 122,000 in May, the largest gain since January last year, above expectations of 117,000 and the previous reading of 109,000. — link

Bankless co-founder David Hoffman stated that after selling all his ETH, he immediately allocated approximately 50% of the funds to VVV, NEAR, ZEC, and HYPE, and used the remaining 50% to purchase LIT.

Previously, he stated that Ethereum has achieved a market capitalization commensurate with its actual performance, but that a significant structural revaluation of ETH as an asset is unlikely in the future. — link

Stripe, Visa and Mastercard are close to launching a new stablecoin platform, while Coinbase is also exploring possible participation, according to CoinDesk. Coinbase, Stripe and Visa declined to comment, and Mastercard had not responded by publication time.

CoinGecko data shows the stablecoin market cap is about $325 billion. Stripe previously acquired stablecoin infrastructure firm Bridge for $1.1 billion, Mastercard acquired BVNK, and Visa expanded its stablecoin settlement pilot to nine blockchains. — link

Prediction market platform Kalshi announced on X that it has launched Bitcoin perpetual contracts. The CFTC previously approved KalshiEX to list the BTCPERP contract, which is tied to the spot price of Bitcoin, saying the product complies with the Commodity Exchange Act and the relevant core principles for designated contract markets (DCMs). Polymarket has also launched invitation-only perpetual contracts and plans to make them fully available to the public in the coming weeks. — link

Largest Ethereum Treasury Company Bitmine Plans 3 Million Shares of 9.50% Perpetual Preferred Stock, Proceeds May Be Used to Acquire Additional ETH

Bitmine Immersion Technologies announced a proposed offering of 3 million shares of 9.50% Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock. The company said net proceeds may be used to acquire additional ETH and other digital assets, expand staking and validator infrastructure including MAVAN, pursue strategic investments related to the Ethereum ecosystem and broader digital asset adoption, fund working capital, and repurchase common stock. — link

FG Nexus Losses on Ethereum Treasury Strategy Top $85 Million

Nasdaq-listed Ethereum treasury firm FG Nexus bought 50,770 ETH for about $196 million at an average price of $3,860 between August and September 2025, before beginning to sell in November. It has now sold 36,025 ETH at an average price of $2,330, recovering about $83.92 million, with cumulative losses on its Ethereum treasury strategy exceeding $85 million. FG Nexus previously described ETH as its primary treasury reserve asset. — link

Bankless Co-Founder Explains Why He Sold All His ETH

Bankless co-founder David Hoffman said in a May 29 interview with Unchained that selling all his ETH was not because he is bearish on Ethereum, nor does he want to be labeled a "defector." He said the decision came down to opportunity cost, as he sees better opportunities elsewhere.

Hoffman noted that Bankless was built around the thesis of Ether as money, but he now believes ETH is difficult to re-rate. In his view, Ethereum lacks the strong coordination and execution needed to regain its unique momentum. — link

Bitcoin Drops Over 16% in a Month While S&P 500 Gains 5%

Charles Schwab’s Jim Ferraioli said Bitcoin’s recent underperformance is less about Strategy’s small BTC sale and more about BTC losing its momentum-trade appeal. BTC has fallen more than 16% over the past month, while the S&P 500 has gained about 5%, as capital rotates into AI, gold, commodities, hot IPOs and other high-momentum assets. — link

Hyperliquid’s May Perps Volume Hits Record 6.63% of Global CEX Total and 14.4% of Binance

Hyperliquid saw its May perps volume rise to a record 6.63% of total global CEX perpetual futures volume and 14.4% relative to Binance, also a new high. The growth was mainly driven by its HIP-3 framework, which generated more than $62 billion in May volume and about $3 billion in open interest, though the report noted that Hyperliquid’s pure crypto perps volume still declined year over year amid broader market weakness. — link

Arthur Hayes Sells HYPE and NEAR, Warns Market May Peak Before September

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes said he has sold all of his HYPE and NEAR holdings and will explain the move in his upcoming essay "Reality Test" next week. Hayes cited rising energy prices from the Iran war and inventory restocking, three major AI IPOs expected this summer through early Q3, and the possibility that Trump may turn against AI to win the midterm elections. He said the market top could arrive sometime between now and September, prompting him to take profits. — link

Spacecoin Announces $100M Vietnam Deal to Build Decentralized Satellite Network

Spacecoin, which describes itself as a satellite-powered DePIN project building decentralized internet connectivity, said it signed an exclusive MoU with Vietnamese technology firm DETI Technology to deploy decentralized satellite communications, sovereign routing, blockchain and edge AI infrastructure in Vietnam. The deployment is centered on serving two of Vietnam’s largest mobile carriers, Mobifone and Gtel. — link

CryptoQuant: BTC Short-Term Holders Show Strongest Capitulation Signal of the Year

According to CryptoQuant, Bitcoin short-term holders have exhibited their strongest capitulation signal of the year. Over the past 24 hours, 53,800 BTC were transferred to exchanges at a loss, while profit-taking inflows dropped to zero, marking the most extreme loss-driven short-term holder transfer event so far this year. In addition, investors who accumulated BTC near the recent highs around $80,000 have been sending coins to exchanges and selling into weakness rather than continuing to hold. — link

Spot Bitcoin ETFs Set Record With 13 Consecutive Days of Net Outflows

Galaxy Research stated that spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a historic streak of 13 consecutive days of net outflows from May 15 to June 3, with cumulative outflows totaling $4.33 billion, equivalent to approximately 59,351 BTC. The recent selling pressure was the most severe on record, with the 7-day ($2.78 billion), 10-day ($3.06 billion), and 20-day ($5.42 billion / 73,080 BTC) rolling outflow windows each setting all-time records for their respective periods. — link

Bitcoin as Collateral for Home Down Payment: First Fannie Mae Mortgage via Coinbase

Coinbase announced that the first mortgage backed by Fannie Mae and collateralized by Bitcoin has been successfully originated in the United States. The loan was originated and is being serviced by Better, with technology infrastructure provided by Coinbase. Coinbase said the product will be rolled out nationwide this summer, offering Bitcoin holders a new mortgage financing option. — link

Plume and EtherFi Launch $100 Million RWA Vault for Institutional Yield

Plume and EtherFi announced a $100 million RWA Vault to offer EtherFi users access to institutional-grade real-world asset yield through Plume’s regulated vault infrastructure. Plume is an Open Finance platform for institutional assets, while EtherFi is a major DeFi yield platform with more than $6 billion in customer deposits. Eligible users will be able to access the RWA yield product directly through the EtherFi app. Plume previously received a Bermuda Monetary Authority license and U.S. SEC transfer-agent approval. — link

Bankless Co-Founder Ryan Sean Adams: Ethereum Is a Failed Project if ETH Fails to Become a Global Store of Value

Bankless co-founder Ryan Sean Adams argued that being bullish on Ethereum but not ETH is a “mental fallacy,” saying Ethereum should be considered a failed project if ETH fails to become a global store of value.

Bankless co-founder David Hoffman disagreed, arguing that Ethereum’s architecture is designed to minimize explicit value capture and that a clear mechanism linking Ethereum’s growth to sustained value accrual for ETH has yet to be demonstrated. — link
